concern_details.detail: Which components handle the registration request, validate personal information and role, manage role-specific data (student ID / librarian identifier), verify validity and uniqueness, and persist the new user, and what is each component's responsibility?
concern_details.why: The right components are drawn and match the code: Registration form, Registration API, Library facade, User manager, User factories, User registry, User accounts, Persistence manager and the database. But the diagram states almost no responsibilities. Only User manager has one, in its note; for every other box the reader has to infer it from the name or open README/inventory.json. Role-specific data is not visible: nothing on the diagram says that StudentFactory sets studentNumber and LibrarianFactory sets internalIdentifierCode, or that the student ID must match [A-Z]\d{8} (UserManager.java:29,177). The diagram also leaves out the form's own blank-field check (Registration.java:126-130), which is validation done before the facade is called. The unique columns on User, Student and Librarian (User.java:21, Student.java:19, Librarian.java:13) act as a second, database-level uniqueness check. The diagram shows nothing of them.

concern_details.detail: What are the interactions and dependencies among the components involved in registration?
concern_details.why: The main path's dependencies are correct and backed by the code (Registration.java:133, AuthenticationController.java:29-30, LibraryFacade.java:39, UserManager.java:77-92, UserRegistry.java:26-67, PersistenceManager.java:19-43). The view does not show how the components work together when data is invalid or already exists, and the request asks for that explicitly. The note says only that errors 'go back to the caller as exceptions'. It does not show RestExceptionHandler (boundary/SpringBoot/RestExceptionHandler.java:15-22), which turns IllegalArgumentException (validation and duplicate errors) into HTTP 400 {error}. It also leaves out the save-failure path: PersistenceManager.save catches the exception, rolls back and returns false (:31-38), then User manager throws a RuntimeException (UserManager.java:93-95). That RuntimeException is not mapped by the handler, so the API returns 500, and the form shows the message (Registration.java:139-141). These are exactly the error-path integration points the tester has to cover.

level_why: At a balanced level, nine boxes grouped in four layers is about right. Each box is a component-sized group of classes, not a single class. Two small points: the two User manager → User registry arrows ('check duplicates', 'save new user') could become one dependency with a combined label, and the layer packages add little. Adding RestExceptionHandler and fuller notes would not take the view past the balanced level.
missing: RestExceptionHandler (@RestControllerAdvice, RestExceptionHandler.java:15-28): it maps IllegalArgumentException/IllegalStateException to 400 with an error body. A save-failure RuntimeException is not mapped, so the API returns 500. This is the main error-path integration point for the REST entry.

The persistence-failure path: PersistenceManager.save rolls back and returns false (PersistenceManager.java:31-38), then User manager throws 'Server error: the user could not be saved' (UserManager.java:93-95). It is in the README but not in the diagram.
The client-side validation in Registration form: blank fields are rejected before the facade is called (Registration.java:126-130). The error is shown with showError (Registration.java:139-141).

Responsibilities and role-specific data on the diagram itself. User factories build a Student with studentNumber or a Librarian with internalIdentifierCode. User registry looks up by email, student number or librarian code. The database's unique constraints on email, studentNumber and internalIdentifierCode back the uniqueness checks.
uml: Dependency notation is mixed. Most relations are drawn as solid open arrows (-->), which in UML read as associations. Only 'stores' is a dashed dependency (..>). Between components, use dependencies (dashed ..>), or required/provided interfaces with assembly connectors.

No provided or required interfaces are shown, even though the viewpoint is component-and-connector and the stakeholder needs integration points. At least the REST interface (POST /api/auth/register), the facade's register operation and User registry's lookup/save operations should be provided interfaces that their clients require.

The database uses a custom stereotype, <<muted>>, together with a legend that says 'Muted box = external system'. Drop the styling stereotype and mark the database as external with a standard notation, for example a node or artifact for the MySQL schema.
fixes: Add RestExceptionHandler to Presentation, with a dependency to Registration API. In a note, show the error paths: validation and duplicate errors as IllegalArgumentException → HTTP 400 (API) or an error dialog (form); save failure (PersistenceManager returns false) as RuntimeException → HTTP 500 or the form message.

Draw component dependencies as UML dependencies (..>), not solid associations. Show the main integration points as provided/required interfaces: REST register, facade register, User registry find/save.

Put each component's responsibility on the diagram, for example in short notes or the component text. Make role-specific data explicit: StudentFactory → studentNumber ([A-Z]\d{8}), LibrarianFactory → internalIdentifierCode, with uniqueness checked by User manager through User registry and backed by unique DB columns.
Show the Registration form's blank-field check as validation that happens before the facade is called.

Merge the two User manager → User registry arrows into one dependency labelled 'check duplicate email/identifier; save'. Replace the <<muted>> stereotype and the legend with standard notation for the external database.
